t: You're at the site of St Michael, Crooked Lane, an ancient parish church that stood on the east side of Miles's Lane, in Candlewick ward of the City. The church is gone now. It was rebuilt after the Great Fire of London by Sir Christopher Wren and then demolished in 1831. Wren was the architect given responsibility for rebuilding fifty-two City churches after the fire of 1666, and he is also known for St Paul's Cathedral, completed in 1710. So this was one of his many City churches, and it survived for a little under two centuries.
